charts/umbrella/Chart.yaml of tractus-x-umbrella, chart version 26.06.01, and its local subcharts

products.name: Tractus-X EDC (connector)
products.description: Control plane and data plane images of the Eclipse Dataspace Components, the connector every participant uses to offer and consume data.
products.scenario: A provider offers an asset under a policy, and a partner finds it in the catalog, negotiates a contract and pulls the data.
products.workshopNote: Runs in the workshop environment: two connectors, their wallets, a Digital Twin Registry and a BDRS.
moreScenarios: A partner without the required credential is refused the contract.
Data is served with a valid EDR token and refused without one.
A push transfer delivers the data to the partner's endpoint.

products.name: Digital Twin Registry
products.description: Registry in which a data provider lists its digital twins (AAS shell descriptors) so that partners can find them.
products.scenario: A twin its owner registers can be read back, and a partner finds and reads it through the owner's connector.
products.workshopNote: Runs in the workshop environment: two connectors, their wallets, a Digital Twin Registry and a BDRS. This is the worked example.
moreScenarios: A partner only sees the twins and identifiers it is allowed to see.
A twin that does not exist is answered with 404.

products.name: Tractus-X IdentityHub (wallet and IssuerService)
products.description: DCP wallet that holds a participant's verifiable credentials, and the IssuerService that issues them.
products.scenario: A participant presents its membership credential in a contract negotiation and is accepted, and a policy asking for a credential it does not hold is refused.
products.workshopNote: Runs in the workshop environment: two connectors, their wallets, a Digital Twin Registry and a BDRS.

products.name: BPN-DID Resolution Service (BDRS)
products.description: Directory that resolves a Business Partner Number (BPN) to the DID of that participant.
products.scenario: A partner's BPN is resolved to its DID, and the partner's catalog is reached with nothing but that BPN.
products.workshopNote: Runs in the workshop environment: two connectors, their wallets, a Digital Twin Registry and a BDRS.

products.name: Tractus-X SDK
products.description: Python libraries for building applications that provide and consume data through the connector, the Digital Twin Registry and the discovery services.
products.scenario: The SDK's connector and registry services complete a provide-and-consume journey against two real connectors.
products.workshopNote: Runs in the workshop environment. TestLab's steps are built on the SDK, so a run exercises it. The repository already has a first TCK under tck/connector.

products.name: Discovery Finder
products.description: Service that tells a participant which BPN Discovery endpoints exist for a given identifier type.
products.scenario: A registered BPN Discovery endpoint is returned for its identifier type, and an unknown type returns an empty list.
products.workshopNote: Small REST API with an OpenAPI document: build and compile in the workshop, run where the service and its identity provider are deployed.

products.name: BPN Discovery
products.description: Service that looks up which Business Partner Numbers (BPN) own a given identifier, for example a manufacturer part ID.
products.scenario: An identifier registered for a BPN is found again by a search, and it is gone after it was deleted.
products.workshopNote: Small REST API with an OpenAPI document: build and compile in the workshop, run where the service and its identity provider are deployed.

products.name: Semantic Hub
products.description: Catalogue of semantic models (SAMM aspect models) and the artifacts generated from them, such as JSON schemas.
products.scenario: A published aspect model is listed, its JSON schema can be generated, and an invalid model is rejected.
products.workshopNote: Small REST API with an OpenAPI document: build and compile in the workshop, run where the service and its identity provider are deployed.

products.name: Business Partner Data Management (BPDM)
products.description: Services that keep the golden record of business partners: the Gate for sharing members, the Pool, and the Orchestrator between them.
products.scenario: A business partner a member uploads to the Gate arrives in the Pool as a golden record with a BPN.
products.workshopNote: Needs BPDM and its identity provider deployed. Build from the Gate and Pool OpenAPI documents in the workshop.

products.name: Portal
products.description: Entry point of a dataspace operator: company registration and onboarding, user and technical user management, app and service marketplace.
products.scenario: An invited company completes its registration, is approved by the operator and can create a technical user.
products.workshopNote: Needs the Portal backend and both identity providers deployed. A long flow: plan more than one session.

products.name: Portal IAM (Keycloak instances)
products.description: Reference configuration of the central and the shared Keycloak identity providers that Portal and the core services log in against.
products.scenario: A technical user gets a token from the central identity provider and a protected service accepts it, and an unknown client is refused.
products.workshopNote: Needs both Keycloak instances deployed. The token request needs client credentials supplied at run time.

products.name: Self-Description Factory
products.description: Service that creates the self-description document of a participant or a connector and has it signed.
products.scenario: A self-description requested for a participant is created, and a request with missing mandatory data is rejected.
products.workshopNote: Needs the service, its identity provider and a signing service deployed.

products.name: SSI Credential Issuer
products.description: Service through which the operator issues verifiable credentials, such as membership and framework agreements, to participants.
products.scenario: A credential requested for a participant is approved by the operator and arrives in the participant's wallet.
products.workshopNote: Needs the issuer, the Portal backend, an identity provider and a wallet deployed.

products.name: SSI DIM Wallet Stub
products.description: Stand-in for a managed wallet service, used so that a dataspace can be run without a commercial wallet.
products.scenario: A wallet is set up for a new participant, and a token it issues is accepted by a connector.
products.workshopNote: Needs the stub and the Portal backend deployed.

products.name: Item Relationship Service (IRS)
products.description: Builds the tree of related digital twins across companies, for example every part built into a vehicle.
products.scenario: A job started for a twin returns the item tree with the twin's child parts, fetched from the partner through the connector.
products.workshopNote: Needs the IRS, a Digital Twin Registry with linked test twins, a submodel server and the discovery services.

products.name: Trace-X (Traceability FOSS)
products.description: Application for tracking parts along the supply chain and for sending quality notifications to partners.
products.scenario: A quality notification sent for a part arrives at the partner, and the partner's reply closes it.
products.workshopNote: Needs Trace-X, the IRS and a full data provider stack deployed on two sides.

products.name: PURIS
products.description: Predictive Unit Real-Time Information Service: partners exchange stock, demand and production data for short-term demand and capacity management.
products.scenario: Stock information a supplier provides for a material is received and shown on the customer side.
products.workshopNote: Needs two PURIS instances, each with a connector and a Digital Twin Registry.

products.name: Industry Core Hub
products.description: Data provision and consumption orchestrator: publishes parts as digital twins and consumes partner data through the connector.
products.scenario: A part published through the hub is found by a partner in the Digital Twin Registry, and its submodel is pulled through the connector.
products.workshopNote: Needs the hub deployed next to the provider's connector and registry. Build from its OpenAPI document in the workshop.

products.name: AAS Suite
products.description: Asset Administration Shell tooling that connects Eclipse BaSyx with the Tractus-X SDK.
products.scenario: A shell and submodel created through the suite are readable by a partner through the connector.
products.workshopNote: Needs the suite deployed next to a connector.

products.name: Knowledge Agents
products.description: Reference implementation of federated queries in dataspaces (CX-0084): agents, the connector extensions and the AAS bridge.
products.scenario: A federated query sent by one participant is answered with data bound from a partner's agent, through both connectors.
products.workshopNote: Needs connectors built with the agent extensions and a provisioning agent on the provider side.

products.name: Tractus-X EDC Kafka Extension
products.description: Connector extension for continuous, event-driven data exchange between companies over Apache Kafka.
products.scenario: A partner negotiates a Kafka asset, receives short-lived broker credentials and reads the messages of the stream.
products.workshopNote: Needs connectors built with the extension and a Kafka broker.

products.name: EDC Dashboard and Policy Builder
products.description: Web interface for a connector's Management API, with a builder for Catena-X policies.
products.scenario: A policy built with the dashboard is created on the connector and is the policy a partner sees in the catalog.
products.workshopNote: A user interface: the test covers the Management API calls behind it, not the clicks.

products.name: Managed Simple Data Exchanger (SDE)
products.description: Convenience layer for data providers and consumers: upload data as CSV or JSON, and the service creates twins, assets and contract offers.
products.scenario: Data uploaded through the exchanger appears as a twin and as a contract offer a partner can negotiate.
products.workshopNote: Needs the exchanger, a Portal with its identity provider, a connector and a registry.

products.name: Managed Service Orchestrator
products.description: Automates the setup of a connector and a Digital Twin Registry for a company that subscribes to them as a managed service.
products.scenario: A subscription triggers the setup, and the connector it deploys answers a catalog request.
products.workshopNote: Needs the orchestrator, a Portal and a cluster it may deploy into.

products.name: E2E Data Exchange Test Service
products.description: Service a participant uses to check that its own connector can exchange data with a partner's.
products.scenario: A test started for a connector reports success for a working connector and a clear failure for an unreachable one.
products.workshopNote: Needs the service deployed with a Portal and its identity provider.

products.name: Dataspace Management
products.description: The modernised portal: a service and a user interface with which an onboarding service provider manages the companies it brings into a dataspace.
products.scenario: A company created by an onboarding service provider can be read back, and a user of another provider cannot see it.
products.workshopNote: Needs the service and its identity provider deployed. Its metafile names a leading repository that does not exist yet.

products.name: Tractus-X SDK Services
products.description: Test orchestrator and digital twin pull service that help a new partner check its setup during onboarding.
products.scenario: The pull service fetches a twin's submodel from a partner through the connector and reports each step it took.
products.workshopNote: Needs both services deployed next to a connector.

products.name: Tractus-X Starter Kit
products.description: Configuration wizard that generates a ready-to-run Docker Compose dataspace for newcomers.
products.scenario: A setup generated with the default answers starts, and its first data exchange succeeds.
products.workshopNote: Runs in Docker Compose, not in the developer toolbox: the workflow needs its own bring-up step.

products.name: Tractus-X TestLab
products.description: The test authoring and execution engine this tutorial uses: declarative YAML tests, compiled into a package and run against real systems.
products.scenario: The compile, validate and run pipeline passes against a live dataspace.
products.workshopNote: Already has its E2E test as a TCK project. Read it as the reference.
